links.outcome: Discrimination of AI early warning scores versus simpler non-AI scores for clinical deterioration on the same data
links.effect: eCART AUROC 0.895 (95% CI 0.891-0.900) vs NEWS2 0.831, NEWS 0.829, RI 0.828, EDI 0.808, MEWS 0.757; NEWS, a non-AI score, significantly outperformed EDI.
links.quote: In this cohort study of inpatient encounters, eCART outperformed the other AI and non-AI scores, identifying more deteriorating patients with fewer false alarms and sufficient time to intervene.

links.outcome: Positive predictive values at thresholds matched to NEWS sensitivity or specificity levels, indicating false alarm burden
links.effect: At the moderate-risk level PPV ranged from 6.3% (EDI 41) to 17.3% (eCART 94); at the high-risk level from 14.5% (EDI 54) to 23.3% (eCART 97).
links.quote: After matching scores at the moderate-risk sensitivity level for a NEWS score of 5, overall positive predictive values (PPVs) ranged from a low of 6.3% (95% CI, 6.1%-6.4%) for an EDI score of 41 to a high of 17.3% (95% CI, 16.9%-17.8%) for an eCART score of 94.

screen.reason: This study performs a large multi-hospital comparative external validation of proprietary AI early warning systems versus simple scores, specifically evaluating alert threshold calibration (matching sensitivity and specificity thresholds) and lead times to manage false alarm rates.
